messages.subject: Prior for Poisson
parts:
I would like to fit a model Y~Poisson(E*lambda), where E are the expected counts. I would like to put a prior on the parameter lambda as Gamma(a,b). Since the Poisson likelihood does not have any hyperparameters listed, is there a way
to fit this model and put a prior on lambda? If yes, are there any examples on how to do it?  I assume control.data does not work since lambda is not a hyperparameter for Poisson.
Thank you,
Georgiana

messages.author: 13c089061b9212a0
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior for Poisson
parts:
In this case lambda is connected to the linear predictor through

log(lambda) = eta

What you could do is to define the linear predictor as a intercept and use the default Normal distribution for the intercept. I mean, use

formula = y ~ 1

and change the prior mean and precision for the intercept with control.fixed. Just to mention this model you described is quite simple and even has closed form solution, see for ex. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution#Bayesian_inference.

Best,
Thiago
